explanation.repair_task: [wasm] Atomic memory.size and dynamic bounds checks for shared memory.
explanation.changed_path: src/wasm/baseline/liftoff-compiler.cc (LiftoffCompiler::BoundsCheckMem) and src/wasm/turboshaft-graph-interface.cc (TurboshaftGraphBuildingInterface::BoundsCheckMem). Both compilers implement the dynamic (explicit) memory bounds check used for shared-memory / atomic / memory64 accesses. The size operand is loaded dynamically at runtime (it can be grown concurrently for shared memories). The check consists of (a) an optional guard that traps when the compile-time constant `end_offset` already exceeds the dynamic memory size, and (b) `effective_size = mem_size - end_offset` followed by `index >= effective_size -> trap`. Guard (a) exists solely to keep the subtraction in (b) from underflowing when `end_offset > mem_size`. The change reworks the elision condition for guard (a) and its comments to talk about the dynamic/shared-memory size.
explanation.introduced_defect: The elision condition for guard (a) was changed from `end_offset > memory->min_memory_size` to `end_offset > memory->max_memory_size` in both Liftoff and Turboshaft. Because the decoder already guarantees `offset + access_size <= max_memory_size` (hence `end_offset < max_memory_size`), the new condition is always false, so guard (a) is never emitted. For any explicitly-bounds-checked access whose constant `end_offset` is greater than the current memory size (but <= the declared maximum), `effective_size = mem_size - end_offset` underflows to a huge value, the `index >= effective_size` comparison passes, and the access proceeds out of bounds. The correct bound is `min_memory_size`, since `mem_size >= min_memory_size` always holds and that is what makes the subtraction safe to elide.
explanation.reachability: Explicit bounds checks are used (force_check) for all atomic memory instructions, and for memory64 when trap handling is unavailable. A shared wasm memory with a small initial size and a large maximum, accessed via `i32.atomic.store` with a large static offset, reaches the buggy path and writes far past the end of the backing store into the reserved PROT_NONE guard region. Non-atomic memory32 accesses are unaffected (they use the trap handler and return before this code).
explanation.poc: pocs/probe.js builds a module with a shared memory (initial 1 page, maximum 1000 pages) and a function doing `i32.atomic.store` at index 0 with static offset 0x100000 (16 pages). The access is 16 pages beyond the committed size but within max_memory_size.

verification.build: gn gen out/x64.asan && ninja -j4 -C out/x64.asan d8
verification.edited_tree: Crashes: 'Received signal 11 SEGV_ACCERR 0x...100000', exit code 139 (fault address matches the 0x100000 offset; the atomic store faults in the guard region).
verification.parent_tree: Clean: prints 'trapped cleanly: RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds', exit code 0 (the dynamic end-offset check correctly traps and the PoC catches it).
verification.regression_check: In-bounds atomic store/load still works and a dynamic out-of-bounds index still traps correctly; only accesses whose static end_offset exceeds the current memory size are affected.
